narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Traditionally danced for the pleasure of Balinese royal families, Condong introduces royal legong, gambuh, and arja theatrical suites.
It portrays the devotion, awe, and daily duties of a palace maidservant serving her sovereign.
Today, it also features in youth dance competitions, preservation festivals, and international conservatory showcases.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The condong dancer enters the stage solo before the legong begins, moving with an intense and sharp dynamic quality.
The routine depicts a capricious maidservant attending to court life and admiring royal majesty.
As the legong performers enter, the condong dancer dances alongside them, hands each a fan, and withdraws.
Watch for Fan presentation, Raven omen dance.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Condong is accompanied by the semar pangulingan style of gamelan, as well as antique ensembles such as the Semara Patangian orchestra.
The musical composition features a sequence of short 16-beat melodic structures played in the gegaboran meter.
Listen for the semar pangulingan gamelan, Semara Patangian gamelan orchestra.
The pulse is 16-beat gegaboran meter shifting to batel meter.

A refined, vibrant Balinese gamelan sound characterized by the crystalline resonance of semar pangulingan metallurgy, executing short 16-beat melodic periods in gegaboran meter that accelerate and transition sharply into the driving batel meter.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The dance is performed on court stages, theater spaces, and modern concert halls.

Dancers wear traditional Balinese court dance attire appropriate for female palace roles, carry hand fans to present to the subsequent dancers, and don raven wings when enacting the omen in Legong Lasem.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Choreographer and teacher Ni Ketut Arini; master instructors Ni Reneng of Kedaton and I.G.A. Susilawati; choreographer I Wayan Berata (who adapted condong movements into Panyembrama in 1971); and dancer Putu Evie Suyadnyani of Mekar Bhuana Conservatory.
The dance originated in Sukawati and is preserved in major Balinese court traditions including Kedaton and Sanur.

Derived from royal 19th-century court dances and legong prototypes; gave rise to the 1971 modern classic Panyembrama choreographed by I Wayan Berata, and continues as a foundational teaching tool in contemporary Balinese conservatories.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Condong is parent of Legong: Condong features simplified versions of legong movements and serves as its traditional introductory preface.
Condong is variant of Legong Lasem: In Legong Lasem (Legong Kraton), the condong dancer returns wearing raven wings to foretell the king's doom.
Condong is child of Panyembrama: Created in 1971 by I Wayan Berata, incorporating adapted movements from Condong and Legong.
Condong is shares music of Gambuh: Shares the condong stock maidservant character.
